title: Interactive: What left a 15-inch footprint? See the original Bigfoot files
excerpt: Open three original Bigfoot files from the U.S. Forest Service, including a 1982 investigation into 15-inch tracks and two Montana accounts.
content:
A wildlife biologist examined 15-inch footprints in a Washington forest. Neighbors in Montana followed a trail of giant prints until it disappeared beneath the trees. And a hunter recalled finding enormous tracks near the remains of an elk.

Those accounts appear in three records the U.S. Forest Service made public. Open a file below for a quick guide to what's inside and a link to the original scan.

The Bigfoot Reading Room

Bigfoot left tracks. The Forest Service left paperwork.

U.S. Forest Service1982 Forest Service investigation The 15-inch footprints Umatilla National Forest · June–July 1982 · 7 pages Summary and PDF Close file

Forest Service wildlife biologist Rodney L. Johnson examined reported tracks in the Mill Creek watershed of Umatilla National Forest in June 1982. The group photographed the prints and made plaster casts. Johnson concluded the tracks were made by something other than a 300-pound-plus, two-footed creature. A month later, U.S. Border Patrol tracker Joel Hardin called them a hoax.

Look for this

The caption under Photograph #2 on page 2 describes a right footprint about 15 inches long and 7 inches wide. On page 7, Hardin calls the tracks "a very clever attempt to perpetrate a hoax."

Open original PDF: 1982 Forest Service investigation, 7 pages

Clark Fork Valley Press2003 Newspaper clipping The trail that disappeared Plains, Montana · Jan. 15, 2003 · 1 page Summary and PDF Close file

The Clark Fork Valley Press reported that an 8-year-old boy found large footprints in fresh snow near a neighbor's sawmill outside Plains, Montana. Neighbors followed them about 100 yards into the woods. Under the trees, where there was little snow and the ground was hard, the prints faded out.

Look for this

A photo caption at the top right of the front page reports a print 16½ inches long and 8½ inches wide. The measurements and sightings are neighbors' accounts as reported by the newspaper. No agency examined these tracks.

Open original PDF: 2003 newspaper clipping, 1 page

Petty Creek1940s Personal recollection Tracks near the elk Petty Creek, Montana · written c. 1980 · 6 pages Summary and PDF Close file

In a local history of Montana's Petty Creek area, Leo T. Kinney recalled going in with three other men to pack out a bull elk. When they arrived, he wrote, only the entrails were left, and a large set of tracks led away through the snow. The following year, he recounted, another hunter came across similar tracks, smelled a strong odor and heard grunting. Kinney noted that no one actually saw an animal.

Look for this

The elk passage is about halfway down page 3, followed by W.W. Schmitz's account. Kinney wrote this around 1980, recalling events from decades earlier.
